title: When ELIZA meets therapists: A Turing test for the heart and mind

paper.authors: S. Gabe Hatch, Zachary T. Goodman, Laura Vowels, H. Dorian Hatch, Alyssa L. Brown, Shayna Guttman, et al.

dependence.note: ChatGPT 4.0 is the 'machine therapist' whose vignette responses compete with 13 human therapists; all three aims (Turing-test identification, common-factors ratings by an N = 830 panel, linguistic comparison) hinge on the ChatGPT-generated texts.

claim.statement: Responses to 18 couple-therapy vignettes generated by ChatGPT 4.0 (engineered prompt, Table 1) were rated higher on the common factors of therapy by a representative US panel (N = 830) than the therapist-written responses (mu = 27.72 vs 26.12; d = 1.63, 95% CI [1.49, 1.78]; Aim 2), and were correctly identified as machine-written only 51.2% of the time vs 56.1% for therapist responses (Table 2; Aim 1). Model-side (Aim 3): ChatGPT responses were longer (IRR = 1.91 [1.81, 2.02]), more positive (d = 0.92 [0.32, 1.52]) and less negative in sentiment (d = -1.04 [-1.61, -0.47]).
claim.metric: Bayesian test of proportions for attribution accuracy; Bayesian regression on the 5-item common-factors sum score (Cohen's d, 95% credible interval); transforEmotion zero-shot sentiment/common-factor probabilities and UDPipe part-of-speech counts (IRR)
claim.original_source: Results, Aims 1-3 and Tables 2-3 of the PLOS Mental Health article (HTML text at external/papers/W4407403557_plain.txt)

protocol.model: 'ChatGPT 4.0' via the ChatGPT web interface, Dec 2023 - early 2024 (expert responses collected over one month after 2023-12-15; panel 2024-03-08..11); snapshot unpinned - the only model reference is OpenAI's 'gpt-4-and-gpt-4-turbo' docs page [24]
protocol.model_status: live model NOT an experimental API arm: the census hit 'gpt-4-turbo' is a documentation URL in the reference list; the served ChatGPT-4 model of that period was a GPT-4 Turbo preview snapshot (dead), behind an undisclosed system prompt
protocol.prompt_source: Table 1 'Engineered prompt' of the paper (rendered only as an image; text not extracted); vignettes in S1 Table / OSF Table S1.docx
protocol.messages: [engineered prompt defining therapeutic alliance, empathy, professionalism, cultural competence, therapeutic technique/efficacy; no length limit] + vignette; several candidate responses were generated and the research team (authors 1-7, 18) voted for the best per vignette (ties by random draw)
protocol.evaluation: Aims 1-2: human panel (CloudResearch, N = 830) - not re-measurable without new participants. Aim 3 (model-side, automatic): transforEmotion (Cross-Encoder DistilRoBERTa zero-shot) sentiment and common-factor probabilities, UDPipe POS counts and length, compared with the 18 fixed therapist responses via Bayesian regression (brms) - re-measurable if the therapist and ChatGPT response texts are available (OSF Table S1.docx / Data 3.12.2024.csv - content not verified).

budget.assumptions: proxy only: 18 vignettes x 3 candidates x 3 seeds; ~600 input tokens (prompt + vignette), ~500 output tokens; scoring with transforEmotion/UDPipe in R is local compute.

judgment.rule: Not judgeable under ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 for the human-rated claims. Proxy rule (Aim 3, if approved): survival if machine responses remain longer (IRR > 1, CI excluding 1) and more positive / less negative in sentiment (d > 0 / d < 0 with CIs excluding 0) than the fixed therapist responses; death if the sign flips.
judgment.notes: Because the human selection step cannot be replicated blind, use all generated candidates (no best-of-n) and report both.

user_checks: Open OSF 8mnsc (view-only link in the paper) and check whether the 18 therapist and 18 ChatGPT response texts and the Table 1 prompt text are available - required for any proxy.
Accept an API proxy arm (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09) for the Aim-3 linguistic comparison, given that the original used ChatGPT's web UI?
Otherwise record the paper as 'human-outcome, web-UI model'.
domain_notes: A 'Turing test' framing: an N = 830 CloudResearch panel rated single written responses to couple-therapy vignettes, outside any therapeutic relationship - the authors flag the lack of therapeutic context as a limitation. The ChatGPT responses were nearly twice as long, and controlling for length/POS erased most transforEmotion differences, so the headline effect is partly a length/style effect. The 13 therapists knew they were competing with ChatGPT.
